query: For multicomponent high-entropy alloys in solid and liquid states at and near their high melting temperatures, what single testable methodological intervention could overcome the inability of EAM references to represent the many atomic configurations of the ab initio liquid? Explain why it should improve reference–target phase-space overlap, predict the reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references, define the applicable composition and temperature ranges, identify supporting evidence from elemental or binary calculations, and specify a decisive free-energy benchmark that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: An active-learning machine learning interatomic potential (MLIP) using high-dimensional descriptors (e.g., SOAP) and trained on comprehensive ab initio liquid configurations near melting will better capture the complex atomic arrangements in multicomponent high-entropy alloy liquids, thereby improving the reference–target phase-space overlap and reducing the thermodynamic integration path mismatch relative to traditional EAM potentials (such as those employed in TOR-TILD).
generation.material_initial_state: Multicomponent high‐entropy alloys with equiatomic or near‐equiatomic compositions, present both in their solid state and in a liquid state exhibiting a wide range of atomic configurations near the high melting temperature.
generation.intervention: Develop and deploy an active-learning MLIP by iteratively training on ab initio MD data sampled at temperatures from 0.9 to 1.1 times the melting temperature, using high-dimensional descriptors to capture many-body interactions.
generation.conditions: The method is applicable to equiatomic or nearly equiatomic multicomponent HEAs in the near-melting regime (approximately 0.9–1.1 Tm), where the liquid phase undergoes extensive configurational diversity.
generation.structural_mediator: The MLIP acts as a mediator by mapping the intricate many-body interactions of the ab initio liquid configurations into a flexible, data-driven potential energy surface that more closely mirrors the target ab initio phase space.
generation.mechanism: Active learning enriches the training dataset by identifying and sampling underrepresented regions of the configurational space. The high-dimensional descriptors ensure subtle many-body interactions are captured, thereby reducing mismatch along the thermodynamic integration path and enhancing phase-space overlap relative to fixed-form EAM potentials.
generation.predicted_outcome: The use of the MLIP is expected to reduce the free-energy integration path mismatch to below approximately 10 meV/atom compared to the errors observed with TOR-TILD’s EAM references, indicating markedly improved phase-space representation of the liquid state.
generation.baseline: Traditional EAM potentials (such as those used in TOR-TILD) that have been shown to inadequately represent the vast configurational diversity in ab initio liquid states, leading to significant thermodynamic integration mismatches.
generation.boundary: This approach is anticipated to be effective for equiatomic or near-equiatomic multicomponent HEAs near melting (0.9–1.1 Tm). Its performance outside this specific composition or temperature regime remains uncertain and requires further validation.
generation.uncertainty: While successes in elemental and binary liquid simulations with MLIPs suggest improvement, there remains uncertainty in fully capturing rare liquid configurations and in the extrapolation of this method to compositions or temperature ranges far outside 0.9–1.1 Tm.

falsification_experiment.design: Train an active-learning MLIP on ab initio MD data for a representative equiatomic HEA within the temperature range of 0.9–1.1 Tm. Perform thermodynamic integration using the MLIP as the reference potential and compare the computed free energies per atom against those obtained from full ab initio thermodynamic integration. Additionally, evaluate statistical measures (e.g., distribution overlap metrics) between the MLIP-sampled configurations and the ab initio phase space.
measurements: Free energy per atom differences (in meV/atom) between the MLIP-based reference and full ab initio calculations
Quantitative statistical metrics (e.g., Kullback-Leibler divergence) of phase-space overlap between the MLIP and ab initio sampling
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the MLIP-based method fails to reduce the thermodynamic integration path mismatch to below ~10 meV/atom or does not exhibit a statistically significant improvement in phase-space overlap over the TOR-TILD EAM reference, then the hypothesis will be considered falsified.

The purpose of this work is to investigate the effect of the Cr content on the microstructure and properties of the WVTaTiCr x coating. The morphologies and phase compositions of five coatings with different Cr contents were comparatively observed. In addition, the hardness and high-temperature oxidation resistance of the coatings were also analyzed. As a result, with the increase in Cr, the coating grains were more refined. All the coating is mainly composed of the BCC solid-solution phase, which promotes the precipitation of the Laves phase with the increase in Cr. The addition of Cr greatly improves the hardness, high-temperature oxidation resistance and corrosion resistance of the coating. The WVTaTiCr (Cr 1 ) exhibited superior mechanical properties, especially in terms of its exceptional hardness, high-temperature oxidation resistance and outstanding corrosion resistance. Abstract High entropy alloy nanoparticles bring hope to developing more efficient nanomaterials for high‐temperature applications. Nevertheless, the enhanced thermal stability of nearly equiatomic nanoalloys containing at least 5 metals is nothing more than theoretical speculation about the impact of thermodynamic contributions on their structural properties and remains to be proven. Here, in situ aberration‐corrected scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) and molecular dynamics simulations are combined to investigate at the atomic scale the thermal behavior of AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles (NPs) from 298 to 973 K. Both in situ STEM heating and atomistic simulations reveal strong structural and chemical evolutions in the NPs with the formation and melting of an AuCu layer at the surface of NPs at high temperature. This phase separation that appears progressively with temperature is driven by pronounced atomic diffusion that is surprisingly more active in these quinary nanoalloys than in monometallic and bimetallic subsystems. decision.trend: Early work in high‐entropy alloy modeling has relied on traditional EAM potentials to simulate material behavior at high temperatures – both in the solid and transient liquidlike regimes. These studies (e.g., in PMC6908586 and PMC11775865) provided valuable insight into defect evolution, diffusion, and phase transformations via MD simulations, yet repeatedly encountered the limitation that standard EAM potentials inadequately sample the vast configuration space of multicomponent liquids. Over time, attempts such as TOR-TILD have sought to bridge the reference–target gap by using EAM-based paths, but these still suffer from notable thermodynamic integration path mismatches because the many-body liquid state configurations are poorly captured. As the community evolved from using fixed functional forms to more sophisticated sampling and multi-scale simulation strategies, the underlying issue – the insufficient phase-space overlap between ab initio liquid states and the simplified reference models – has remained unresolved.
decision.unsolved: The key unsolved challenge is to construct a single simulation reference that reliably represents the extreme configurational complexity of ab initio liquids in multicomponent high-entropy alloys near melting. This results in a residual thermodynamic integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references, leading to inaccuracies in computed free energies. No intervention to date has both expanded the sampled configuration space and been quantitatively benchmarked against ab initio integration targets in this regime.
decision.lever: Develop an active-learning machine learning interatomic potential (MLIP) based on high-dimensional descriptors (e.g., SOAP or similar) that is trained on a comprehensive set of ab initio liquid configurations sampled near the high melting temperatures of multicomponent HEAs.
decision.why: This approach directly attacks the root cause—the inability of classical EAM potentials to cover the liquid’s many atomic configurations—by building a flexible and data-rich potential energy model. It is a logical extension of recent successes in elemental and binary liquid simulations where MLIPs have demonstrated markedly improved accuracy in phase-space representation. Moreover, by benchmarking the MLIP’s free-energy predictions against ab initio thermodynamic integration (with a tolerable deviation, e.g., <10 meV/atom), one can decisively test the hypothesis. The method is applicable to HEAs in the near-melting regime (approximately 0.9–1.1 Tm) for typical equiatomic or near equiatomic multicomponent systems.
